newsitem.title: COLOMBIA: Colombian rebels blast main oil pipeline again.
newsitem.headline: Colombian rebels blast main oil pipeline again.

text.p: Leftist rebels dynamited a section of Colombia's largest oil pipeline on Thursday causing all pumping operations to cease, police sources said.

The attack on the 500 mile (780 km) pipeline took place near the town of Carmen in northeast Norte de Santander. Police blamed the blast on guerrillas of the National Liberation Army ELN, the country's second largest rebel force set up by radical Roman Catholic priests in the mid-1960s.

The pipeline pumps about 220,000 barrels of crude a day from the field operated by U.S. multinational Occidental Petroleum Corp near the northeast town of Cano Limon to the lifting terminal on the Caribbean coast at Covenas.

Police were unable to give any estimate of the amount of crude spilled. Last year rebels blew up the pipeline 47 times, causing the loss of 105,000 barrels of crude and costing state-run oil company Ecopetrol more than $9 million.
Colombia's army commander Gen. Manuel Jose Bonett, meanwhile, accused the ELN of infiltrating the country's main oil workers' union, in an interview with the NTC TV news programme.
"Of course the union is infiltrated by guerrillas, that's been shown," Bonett said.
The USO oil workers union is currently negotiating with Ecopetrol to avert a threatened all-out strike, which could paralyse the state-run oil sector.

The union is demanding an end to plans to split Ecopetrol's gas operations into a separate company, calling for 2,000 workers to be taken on and an end to the legal persecution of a handful of its members in custody on charges of links with terrorist groups.
The USO has said it will break off talks if no agreement is reached by Friday. Previous fears that a strike was imminent have, however, proved unfounded.
